ledger.note: 1748: Nawab Bahawal Khan I establishes Bahawalpur. The infobox 'Established 1748, by Nawab Bahawal Khan Abbasi, who had migrated from Shikarpur, Sindh'; the city page: it 'replaced Derawar as the clan's capital city'. The city page also says the princely state 'was founded in 1802' by Bahawal Khan II after the Durrani Empire broke up, and the ruler table starts in 1689; the region is the researcher's reading of the Bahawalpur country (45,911 km2 in 1809).

ledger.note: 1847-48: Sabzalkot and Bhung. The Nawab 'helped Herbert Edwardes's expedition against Multan and was rewarded with Sabzalkot and Bhung'. The page does not name the former holder (the Sikh Empire's Multan province, on the reading that Edwardes's reward came out of the campaign); 1848 is the year of the Multan campaign. [Reviewer sa-06-x, 2026-10-25: counterpart changed from sikh-empire to east-india-company: the state page says the Nawab 'was rewarded by the grant of the districts of Sabzalkot and Bhung' for his help in the First Anglo-Afghan War and the 1847-48 expedition against Multan, i.e. a British grant; the drawn disc (70.1 E 28.3 N) lies in upper Sindh, Company land since 1843, not in the Sikh province of Multan. east-india-company should record the matching loss.]

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 by sa-06-x. A state Cliopatria lacks: cliopatria_names empty, every keyframe new. Two pages opened for the state (Bahawalpur (princely state), Bahawalpur) and Company rule in India (already read for east-india-company) for the 1858 transfer; WebFetch returned extracts. The 'Abbasi dynasty' page does not exist under that title (url_not_found).

Founding: 1748 (infobox) is used; the city page says the princely state 'was founded in 1802' by Bahawal Khan II when the Durrani Empire broke up, and the ruler table runs from 1689 (pre-state emirs), with Bahawal Khan I's reign from 1743. No page says whether Bahawalpur was a Durrani vassal before 1802 (the city page has a Durrani attack in 1785), so no vassal pair is recorded for the Durranis. The 1809 Treaty of Amritsar is named only as the date of the 45,911 km2 area. The Sikh pressure of 1807 (Multan) is in the city page without a territorial result.

Shape: the state is drawn from named towns (Bahawalpur, Rahim Yar Khan, Derawar Fort, Bahawalnagar) on the grid at about 42,000 km2 (ratio 0.91 to 45,911 km2); Sabzalkot and Bhung (1847-48) lie inside the Sadiqabad area. No page dates the earlier growth, Ahmadpur East, Khanpur or the Derawar and Marot forts. Accession date: 5 October agreement and 9 October acceptance (state page) or 7 October (city page).

Counterparts: east-india-company (written by this batch), sikh-empire, islamic-republic-of-pakistan (another part of sa-06) and british-raj. Gazetteer names absent: Derawar (71.33 E 28.77 N), Bahawalnagar (73.25, 29.99), Sabzalkot/Bhung (70.1, 28.3).

Suzerainty events kept out of the ledger: vassal_start and vassal_end belong in the suzerain's dossier with this state as the counterpart (the schema: 'counterpart is the vassal itself'), so they are listed here for whoever writes or checks the suzerain. 1833-02 vassal_start (suzerain east-india-company, confidence 3, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahawalpur_(princely_state)): 22 February 1833: the subsidiary alliance with the Company. The Nawab 'entered a subsidiary alliance with the British, becoming a princely state'; the treaty 'secured the independence of the Nawab within his own territories' (the Company page: 'Bahawalpur accepts British Suzerainty (1833)'). | 1858-11 vassal_end (suzerain east-india-company, confidence 2, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Company_rule_in_India): 1 November 1858: the Company's rights pass to the Crown ('Nationalisation of the Company and assumption of direct administration by the British Crown: 1 November 1858'); the state itself continues. | 1858-11 vassal_start (suzerain british-raj, confidence 2, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Company_rule_in_India): 1 November 1858: Bahawalpur a princely state under the Crown (British Raj). | 1947 vassal_end (suzerain british-raj, confidence 1, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahawalpur_(princely_state)): 1947: British paramountcy lapses. The page does not date it; it gives the accession agreement of 5 October 1947 (accepted 9 October) and the city page 7 October 1947, so the year is the bridge. | 1947-10 vassal_start (suzerain islamic-republic-of-pakistan, confidence 3, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahawalpur_(princely_state)): October 1947: Bahawalpur accedes to Pakistan. 'The Nawab signed an agreement with the government of Pakistan on 5 October 1947, accepted on 9 October 1947, making Bahawalpur the first state to accede' (the city page says 7 October); it kept its Nawab and a prime minister until 1955. | 1955-10 vassal_end (suzerain islamic-republic-of-pakistan, confidence 3, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahawalpur_(princely_state)): 14 October 1955: merged into West Pakistan.
